newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada carriers reach pilot deals.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada carriers reach pilot deals.

text.p: Air Canada's regional carriers in Ontario and Quebec have reached tentative agreements with striking pilots to end a two-month labor dispute.
Quebec-based Air Alliance reached an agreement with 145 members of the Air Line Pilots Association of Canada on Sunday.

"We'll be convening our members to a general meeting in just a few days in order to present the agreement and we will recommend a ratification," Vincent Charron, president of ALPA local 218, said in a statement.
Air Ontario, which serves central Canada and the northeastern United States, said a deal was reached with 265 pilots late on Saturday night. The details of the contract were not disclosed.
"We are looking forward to having our own fleet back in the air," Air Ontario president Stephen Smith said in a statement released on Sunday.
Air Ontario has been using charter aircraft since the strike began in January.
Union spokesman Kevin Hackett told Reuters a ratification vote at Air Ontario would be held on Tuesday. Air Ontario is still negotiating with 146 striking flight attendants.
Striking pilots at Air B.C. reached an agreement with the British Columbia-based carrier last weekend. Pilots at Air Nova, Air Canada's regional carrier in Atlantic Canada, settled last Tuesday.
About 800 pilots at Air Canada's four regional carriers went on strike Jan. 10.
